title: One chart, one paragraph, one decision
brief:
You are turning an improving caesarean-section SSI run chart into a one-page {{board}}. The page has one chart (the run chart, with the checklist change annotated) and one short paragraph of commentary. All that remains is the closing **decision-asked** sentence — the single line that tells leadership exactly what you want them to do.

A strong decision-ask names one action (one verb) and one time horizon.

task.stem: Which closing decision-asked sentence is strongest?

options.label: ‘The data shows encouraging progress and the team has worked very hard this quarter.’
‘We ask the {{exec}} to endorse continuing the theatre-checklist routine for the next six months, and to review it against this same chart at month 37.’
‘We should probably keep doing what we are doing and maybe look at it again at some point.’
‘We recommend endorsing the checklist, expanding it to two more theatres, hiring an audit clerk, buying a new steriliser, and revising the antibiotic policy.’

debrief.correct: Yes. The **One Chart · One Paragraph · One Decision** structure ends with a decision-asked sentence that has **one verb** (‘endorse’) and **one time horizon** (‘six months, review at month 37’). Leadership knows precisely what is being asked and cannot drift into a generic conversation. The other options fail predictably: the first states progress but asks for nothing; the third is vague with no verb or horizon; the fourth bundles five asks, so the board can approve the easy ones and quietly drop the rest.
debrief.wrong: A board one-pager exists to produce a decision. The strongest closing line names **one action and one time horizon** — ‘endorse continuing the routine for six months, review at M37.’ A sentence that only praises the team asks for nothing; a vague ‘maybe look again’ has no verb or horizon; a five-part shopping list lets the board cherry-pick. One chart, one paragraph, one decision.
debrief.rule_cited: One Chart · One Paragraph · One Decision — executive-friendly reporting; communicating data for a decision — Provost & Murray ch. 7; NAHQ HQCF (Professional Engagement).
